items.label: Adult male
items.statement: Adult males have a brown to chestnut head and neck, black body, reddish-orange bill and casque, and yellow facial skin.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Rufous-headed Hornbill account (uses IUCN 2018 treatment)
items.scopeLimit: 2018 account description, sex and age affect plumage

items.label: Adult female
items.statement: Adult females have a predominantly black head and body with blue facial skin and pouch.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Rufous-headed Hornbill account (uses IUCN 2018 treatment)
items.scopeLimit: 2018 account description, sex and age affect plumage

items.label: 2025 global assessment
items.statement: BirdLife lists the Rufous-headed Hornbill as Endangered under IUCN criterion C2a(ii) in the 2025 assessment.
items.source: BirdLife International DataZone, Rufous-headed Hornbill factsheet, last IUCN assessment 2025
items.scopeLimit: 2025 global IUCN assessment, not national DENR classification

items.label: Breast patch and wings
items.statement: White underparts carry a vivid blood-red breast patch; grey-blue wing-coverts have dark reddish-brown bars.
items.source: IUCN Red List 2024, Gallicolumba luzonica assessment

items.label: Midbody scale rows
items.statement: The 2019 Philippine snake key reports 21–23 longitudinal scale rows at midbody.
items.source: Weinell, Hooper, Leviton & Brown (2019), Illustrated Key to the Snakes of the Philippines, Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 66(1):1–49
items.scopeLimit: Identification-key diagnosis requires examined scale counts

items.label: Color in published key
items.statement: The key distinguishes this cobra by a uniform light-brown or olive dorsum from the darker southern species.
items.source: Weinell, Hooper, Leviton & Brown (2019), Illustrated Key to the Snakes of the Philippines, Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 66(1):1–49
items.scopeLimit: Identification-key diagnosis requires examined scale counts

items.label: Midbody scales and dorsum
items.statement: The 2019 Philippine snake key gives 17–19 midbody scale rows and a dark brown or black dorsal surface.
items.source: Weinell, Hooper, Leviton & Brown (2019), Illustrated Key to the Snakes of the Philippines, Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 66(1):1–49
items.scopeLimit: Identification-key diagnosis requires examined scale counts

items.label: Anterior ventral band
items.statement: The published key notes yellow anterior ventrals followed by a dark band and 162–178 ventral scales.
items.source: Weinell, Hooper, Leviton & Brown (2019), Illustrated Key to the Snakes of the Philippines, Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 66(1):1–49
items.scopeLimit: Identification-key diagnosis requires examined scale counts

items.label: Flippers and tail
items.statement: Dugongs have paddle-like foreflippers, a whale-like fluked tail and no dorsal fin.
items.source: Marsh (2009), Dugong: Dugong dugon, Encyclopedia of Marine Mammals, second edition, pp.332–335
items.scopeLimit: Global external anatomy, not a Philippine occurrence report

items.label: Downturned muzzle
items.statement: The broad flattened muzzle ends in a downturned mouth used to graze marine vegetation.
items.source: Marsh (2009), Dugong: Dugong dugon, Encyclopedia of Marine Mammals, second edition, pp.332–335
items.scopeLimit: Global external anatomy, not a Philippine occurrence report
